```{python}
import polars as pl
import requests
import io
import json
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

# Load the flights JSON data
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
response = requests.get(url)
df = pl.read_json(io.BytesIO(response.content))

print("Shape:", df.shape)
print("Columns:", df.columns)
```


```{python}
# ── Clean the data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Identify numeric delay columns
numeric_cols = [c for c in df.columns 
                if c.startswith("num_of") or c.startswith("minutes_delayed")]

# 1. Replace "n/a" in month with null
df = df.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("month") == "n/a")
      .then(None)
      .otherwise(pl.col("month"))
      .alias("month")
)

# 2. Replace -999 and "1500+" in all numeric delay columns with null,
#    then cast to Float64
for col in numeric_cols:
    df = df.with_columns(
        pl.when(
            pl.col(col).cast(pl.Utf8).is_in(["-999", "1500+"])
        )
        .then(None)
        .otherwise(pl.col(col).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False))
        .alias(col)
    )

# 3. Fill minutes_delayed columns with each column's median
minutes_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith("minutes_delayed")]
fill_minutes = [
    pl.col(c).fill_null(pl.col(c).median()).alias(c)
    for c in minutes_cols
]

# 4. Fill num_of columns with each column's mean
num_of_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith("num_of")]
fill_num_of = [
    pl.col(c).fill_null(pl.col(c).mean()).alias(c)
    for c in num_of_cols
]

df = df.with_columns(fill_minutes + fill_num_of)

# Verify no nulls remain in numeric columns
print("Nulls in num_of columns:", df.select(num_of_cols).null_count().sum_horizontal().item())
print("Nulls in minutes columns:", df.select(minutes_cols).null_count().sum_horizontal().item())

# Also cast num_of_flights_total to Float64
df = df.with_columns(pl.col("num_of_flights_total").cast(pl.Float64))
```

QUESTION 1 — Which Delay Is the Worst?
```{python}
# ── Calculate overall proportions for each delay type ─────────────────────────
total_flights = df["num_of_flights_total"].sum()

summary = df.select([
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").sum()  / total_flights * 100).alias("Carrier (%)"),
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft").sum() / total_flights * 100).alias("Late Aircraft (%)"),
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_security").sum() / total_flights * 100).alias("Security (%)"),
])

print("Overall proportion of flights delayed by each cause:\n")
print(summary)

# ── Unpivot the summary table for plotting ────────────────────────────────────
summary_long = summary.unpivot(
    variable_name="delay_type",
    value_name="proportion"
)

summary_long

# ── Bar chart with labels showing exact percentages ───────────────────
# First, create a label column
summary_long = summary_long.with_columns(
    (pl.col("proportion").round(2).cast(pl.Utf8) + "%").alias("label")
)

plot1 = (
    ggplot(summary_long, aes(x="delay_type", y="proportion", fill="delay_type"))
    + geom_bar(stat='identity')
    + geom_text(aes(label="label"), nudge_y=0.3, size=8, color="black")
    + scale_fill_manual(values=["#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c"])
    + labs(
        title="Which Delay Type Affects the Most Flights?",
        subtitle="Overall proportion of flights delayed by carrier, late aircraft, and security",
        x="Delay Type",
        y="Proportion of All Flights (%)"
    )
    + theme_minimal()
    + theme(legend_position="none")
)
plot1.show()
```

Results:
The most delayed flights due to late arrivals amount to about 6.68% of all the flights. The second-highest type of delay is carrier delay, which accounts for only 4.16%. Security delays make up a very small percentage of total delays (0.03%). The above conclusion seems quite logical because a late arrival impacts the departure of the flight in question, while security delays occur less frequently and last not more than a few minutes. Therefore, when the booking CEO tries to aid their customers in avoiding delays, on-time arrivals should be taken into account.

QUESTION 2 — Delay Proportions Across Airports
```{python}
# ── Calculate proportions by airport ──────────────────────────────────────────
airport_summary = df.group_by("airport_code").agg([
    pl.col("num_of_flights_total").sum().alias("total_flights"),
    pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").sum().alias("carrier"),
    pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft").sum().alias("late_aircraft"),
    pl.col("num_of_delays_security").sum().alias("security"),
])

airport_summary = airport_summary.with_columns([
    (pl.col("carrier")      / pl.col("total_flights") * 100).alias("Carrier (%)"),
    (pl.col("late_aircraft") / pl.col("total_flights") * 100).alias("Late Aircraft (%)"),
    (pl.col("security")     / pl.col("total_flights") * 100).alias("Security (%)"),
])

airport_summary.select(["airport_code", "Carrier (%)", "Late Aircraft (%)", "Security (%)"])

# ── Unpivot for grouped bar chart ─────────────────────────────────────────────
airport_long = airport_summary.unpivot(
    on=["Carrier (%)", "Late Aircraft (%)", "Security (%)"],
    index="airport_code",
    variable_name="delay_type",
    value_name="proportion"
)

airport_long

# ── Grouped bar chart: delay proportions by airport ───────────────────────────
plot2 = (
    ggplot(airport_long, aes(x="airport_code", y="proportion", fill="delay_type"))
    + geom_bar(stat='identity', position='dodge')
    + scale_fill_manual(
        values=["#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c"],
        labels=["Carrier", "Late Aircraft", "Security"]
    )
    + labs(
        title="Delay Proportions by Airport",
        subtitle="Carrier vs. Late Aircraft vs. Security delays across all 7 airports",
        x="Airport",
        y="Proportion of Total Flights (%)",
        fill="Delay Type"
    )
    + theme_minimal()
)
plot2.show()
```

Results:
The phenomenon of late aircraft is pervasive at all airports; however, there is variation in the extent. ORD (Chicago O'Hare International Airport) and SFO (San Francisco International Airport) have the largest share of delays, while SLC (Salt Lake City International Airport) and SAN (San Diego International Airport) have relatively smaller delays. Delay due to carriers is relatively equal at all airports ranging from 5% to 7%. Delays due to security checks are almost zero at all airports, suggesting that this factor is not responsible for delays.
